Ilen not Illen

The name is the banks of the Ilen, (pronounced eye len) not Illen, named after the river which runs through Skibbereen in Co. Cork.

↳ Posted by cathycook on September 1st, 2008.

Nmaes…

Why does this tune have 7 alternative names, with justification for none of them ?

↳ Posted by Kenny on September 1st, 2008.

The Banks of the Ilen:

with one ‘l’ only, it is the name of the river that runs through Skibbereen in West Cork where ‘stands’ of anglers can be spotted trying to catch a peal (a local word for ‘a young salmon on its first return from the sea’)
http://www.riverilen.com/river.htm
An Aighlinn: http://www.logainm.ie/

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on May 10th, 2010.

There seem to be v little ‘justification’ for tune titles on the whole, Kenny… There seem to be some local logic here as Cártaí is an other Cork sounding name and Sixmiletown isn’t far away, just north of the Shanon estuary, in Co Clare. Names can be entered anonymously, but this liberty has rarely been abused, it seems.

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on May 10th, 2010.

As for the various spellings they are justified because they help the automatic listing of ‘tunes recorded under such names’. eg; ‘Seanbhean Na GCarta’ leads to a Caoimhin O’Raghallaigh rendition of The Banks of the Ilen, etc.

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on May 10th, 2010.

Илен?

More ‘Banks of the …’ tunes from the “Music of the Tatar People” CD; a rare collection of songs collected by Laszlo Vikar on the banks of the Volga; this other home of seán-nós!

The Banks Of The Ilen/Dillane’s

Martin Mulvihill recorded this under the title “Dillane’s” after fiddler Tom Dillane, from whom he learned the tune.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 16th, 2013.

The Banks Of The Ilen/Dillane’s

I said, “Martin Mulvihill recorded this under the title ”Dillane’s“ after fiddler Tom Dillane, from whom he learned the tune…” Tried to delete it, but no go. It’s a different tune - sorry.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 16th, 2013.

The Banks Of The Ilen/Dando Dillane’s

From sleeve notes: Martin Mulvihill recorded this under the title “Dando Dillane’s” after a flute player in the parish of Glin, Limerick. Dando was apparently one of the first musicians Martin heard playing that tune.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on June 16th, 2013.

The Banks of The ILEN, X:4

The version taught and played by Co. Cork fiddler, Seamus Creagh, who lived not far from the west Cork market town of Skibbereen, through which the tidal River Ilen flows.

↳ Posted by Larke on August 14th, 2020.

The Banks Of The Ilen, X:5

Transcribed from Star Above The Garter by Denis Murphy And Julia Clifford. The main repeated phrase where it goes deff sometimes goes defd, and possibly they are playing both simultaneously. Chord in B part is not always played, and not 100% whether it is played as a chord on the fiddle or harmonising.
